A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SWE-Search, with matching methods, benchmarks and retained analyses. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are sufficiently readable for a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SWE-bench Lite experiments across five models, search-depth and solution-selection analyses, and supplementary trajectory evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds API-cost reporting and a comparison against five-run Moatless-Adapted results.

M1.justification: The flexible Action Agent, quantitative and qualitative Value Agent, modified UCT search, and debate-based discriminator remain the same. Expanded prompts and baseline descriptions document existing components without establishing an altered method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate repository-level bug fixing on the same 300-instance SWE-bench Lite dataset. The introduction's revised benchmark name clarifies coverage already specified in v1. The added cost and repeated-attempt comparisons introduce no new dataset or task.

E2.justification: Appendix J/Table 4 adds Moatless-Adapted to the Pass@5 comparison; v1's Figure 3 reported only SWE-Search at that metric. Table 1 retains its comparators. Renaming Moatless-v1 to Moatless-v0.0.2 clarifies the baseline version rather than establishing a new comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix J introduces a comparison between five candidates generated within one SWE-Search run and five solutions generated across five Moatless-Adapted runs. GPT-4o is excluded from this additional baseline evaluation for cost reasons. Existing benchmark settings and search limits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices I-J add targeted analyses of API-cost tradeoffs and search performance against repeated baseline attempts. Existing feedback examples, search-depth analysis, loop-escape case study, model-complementarity analysis and value-function diagnostics are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix J explicitly reports one SWE-Search run versus five Moatless-Adapted runs for its comparison. This adds run-count information and a repeated-run design, without establishing increased repetitions of the earlier experiments. Figure 8's standard-deviation reporting is unchanged; no new confidence intervals or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: Table 4 newly reports Moatless-Adapted Pass@5 scores of 17.0, 22.3, 22.0 and 21.7 for GPT-4o-mini, Qwen, DeepSeek and Llama, respectively. Table 3 adds API costs, including $40.86 versus $576.00 for GPT-4o; Qwen and Llama costs are estimates. Earlier benchmark scores and diagnostic findings are retained.

T1.justification: The history-dependent objective, value function and modified UCT equations remain substantively unchanged. Added action-type indices make the previously described hierarchy explicit, without introducing new mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central contribution of combining MCTS, qualitative feedback and debate, the reported 23% improvement across five models, and the claim that performance scales with inference-time search. The added evidence does not redefine these principal claims.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges higher computational costs and the cost-driven omission of GPT-4o from the added comparison. Section 3.5 also explains how debate can distinguish implementations with similar value estimates. Earlier interpretations of feedback, scaling and model diversity remain.

D1.justification: Appendix G replaces a condensed edit-state prompt and worked input example with detailed prompts for Search, Plan, RequestMoreContext and Edit. New appendices provide discriminator prompts, baseline transition/configuration details, API-cost information and interactive-demo access instructions. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation; the original hyperparameter table is retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Coulom (2007) as an MCTS reference in Section 2 and the bibliography. The broader positioning relative to search algorithms and software-agent frameworks remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits include rewriting the abstract's motivation, standardizing baseline names, clarifying type notation, reordering component descriptions and shortening the discriminator discussion while promoting it to Section 3.5. Additional appendix sections organize the new material; the main narrative remains substantially intact.

P2.justification: The prompt presentation is substantially redesigned: v1's two gray monospaced panels are replaced by structured, color-coded state-specific prompt boxes, with additional debate panels in Appendix L. Two new comparison tables are added. Existing scientific figures are retained with only limited surrounding layout changes.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reproducibility through fuller prompts and makes performance-cost tradeoffs more assessable through Appendices I-J. The additional evaluation remains limited: compute matching is briefly specified and excludes GPT-4o. The existing Llama Pass@1 inconsistency also persists—21.0 in Figure 3 versus 17.7 in Table 1 and the new Table 4. These additions provide useful refinement without substantially changing the paper's central evidence.
